note: Misses every stated criterion, and the not_deconditioned exclusion almost verbatim. The ICP quote says 'It's not like we have dudes who come here who are 50 pounds overweight, who are just like, I need to just lose weight' — this prospect opened with 'I really want to lose weight. Specifically, want to lose body fat. I think my body fat is too high' and is 225 lb at 5'10" targeting 190. He is a salaried corporate accountant still studying for his CPA, not a business owner or physician. On income he could not reach the price, is paying down credit card debt and has a 690 credit score. Health is not a neglected-but-fine area either — his doctor has recommended cholesterol medication, which puts him nearer rescue than maintenance, and 'good to great' is not the frame at all: he is trying to get back to a 2018 baseline. Two things make this a useful data point rather than just a bad-fit call. First, he is high-intent and high-character — he committed 100% before hearing the price and validated the product after refusing it — so the filter that should have caught him is a qualification filter, not a desire filter. Second, nothing in the stated ICP would have stopped this call being booked, because the ICP is not applied at set time; it is only visible as a post-hoc explanation of why the call lost.
